BRYANSTON BREAK-INS

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A posh Jo’burg suburb is being targeted in a series of break-ins by gunwielding criminals who appear to be acting on information from the very security company meant to protect resident – we inves

Unique Selling Point:
- CCTV FOOTAGE
- CLEAR PATTERN LINKING A NATIONAL SECURITY COMPANY
- OPPORTUNITY TO TAKE ON COMPANY & COPS

Summary:
Seven Robberies in 5 weeks. All in Bryanston. All between 19.00 & 20.00 at night. All no forced entry. All access gained via keypad or locking mechanism at the remote gate. All ADT Security clients.

It appears that there is a leak within the security company. We investigate, connect the dots and put ADT and the cops in the hotseat.

Further information:
Out of 10 robberies since the middle of September in Bryanston – 7 of the incidents were clients of ADT Security – there was no forced entry and the criminals enter the properties using codes on the keypad at the remote gates of the properties. The conclusion is that information is being leaked from ADT.

All these incidents happen between 19.00 & 20.00 – most people have just had dinner and have not armed the security alarm system yet for the night.

In some incidents the victims have been injured. A man’s hand was broken, another was shot in the shoulder and a third man had his skull cracked and had to undergo surgery.

The criminals usually wear balaclavas, come in with guns, demand electronics, money, jewellery and have made off with two cars from the properties they have robbed.

CASE STUDY 1: KAREN BOUIC
16 Sept 2019 – Karen was held up with her family – the gang came in around 19.30, they gained access using the keypad on the gate. They spent 45 minutes in the house and got away with electronics, jewelry, clothes and took Karen’s Hyundai i20. They suspect it was inside job.
FROM HER HUSBAND:
I had the traumatic event of having five armed men wearing balaclavas enter our house and hold us hostage for 45 minutes. I was beaten when I went to show them where the safe was and the one violent individual jumped on my hand and broke a metacarpal. I had to have four pins put in to hold it together. I cannot begin to tell you how this affected everyone and what thoughts went through my family’s minds during the 45 minutes where these robbers ransacked the house. The point of this story is that these guys entered our property by using our keypad at the gate. We were guarded by Fidelty-ADT and, two events took place in the previous weeks of the armed robbery. Our alarm went off two weeks prior and an ADT security guard came onto our premises whilst we were not at home. Four days before the incident, we called ADT in to do some additional work on the alarm system and the salesperson (Mark Schoeman) wrote up a contract where he transcribed our Digipad code onto the sales document. We never gave him that code, so the implication is that this information is freely available within their organization. We have met with ADT over 3 weeks ago and they agreed to do polygraph tests on their staff which has now come back negative. There have now been five armed and violent incidents in the Bryanston area in the last four weeks where the mode of operation has been to access the property using the keypad. We know with certainty that three of the properties were guarded by ADT who ad access to the gate codes, and we are still to confirm the other two.

CASE STUDY 2: AMY VAN HEERDEN
This happened in Bryanston, 51 Saint James Crescent on Monday 14 Oct 20:05. The perps went through the main complex gate by using the ADT digipad (Video 1). They then went to the top house (house number 1 is at the top) and entered another gate also using the digipad. In Video 2 you can see the 4 perps passing Amy’s gate and digipad (2nd house in the complex) with no interest. The criminals went straight for Unit 1 – it is clear it was a targeted incident. The alarm at unit 1 was already armed when the criminals tried to gain access. They eventually retreated - they left after the alarm was triggered, opening the main gate again with the digipad. There are 4 houses in the complex, with 3 of them using ADT.

THIS IS AN EXAMPLE OF A TARGETED ROBBERY ATTEMPT – THE ROBBERS CAME IN AND HEADED STRAIGHT FOR THE HOUSE THAT THEY HAD THE KEYPAD FOR. THIS INFO HAS BEEN SHARED WITH ADT BY THE CLIENTS, TO DATE NO RESPONSE.

ADT KNOW ABOUT THE ISSUE
ADT are aware of the possible breach – but it appears nothing is being done. No notifications have been sent out to clients informing them of the possible breach or advising them to change their access codes. The robberies continue – just last week there were two.

ADT admitted to one victim that they were aware of the issue and advised him not the give his new access codes to the ADT control centre.

ADT’s RESPONSE TO KAREN BOUIC:
“All employees interviewed and polygraphed, at this stage, denied any involvement in the incident whatsoever and were found to be truthful when answering the relevant questions and advised by the investigator that they be excluded as suspects during any further investigation into the matter.

Regarding the process pertaining to digipad code access during activations, upon receipt of an activation the customer’s digipad access code can only be accessed after entering the customer’s password into the system. The Control Room Operator has to obtain the password from the customers. Once a Reaction Officer is dispatched to the premises the digipad access code is displayed on the vehicle unit (Tom-Tom) in order for the officer to gain access. Once the activation is cancelled or completed the access code is no longer visible to the officer. This process ensures that codes are kept secure.”

BUT it is possible that the code can be written down, a picture can be taken or someone in the control room could have given out the info as they have access to the codes.

The majorit of the 7 ADT cases had a false alarm of sorts in the weeks leading up to the robberies.

CASE STUDY 3: KEGAN MURPHY
In 2018 Kegan Murphy was robbed, also Bryanston. The criminals gained access during the day using a master key for the remote gate that was in the possession of ADT Security. His helper, gardener and 5 year old daughter were held up in the home. Arrests were made, after ADT Security ID-ed one of the men as an ex-ADT employee. He is currently on trial. Kegan is furious – ADT management admitted responsibility and offered to pay for the replacement lock. His daughter has had to go to play therapy following the traumatic incident.

SINCE 2018 ADT HAVE BEEN AWARE OF SECURITY BREACHES.

THE COPS
There at least two other gangs at work in the area at the moment as well. The other gangs access by breaking the gates or jumping walls, they crawl across the gardens under the security beams and then usually remove windows to get into the house.

There have also been other robberies not linked to ADT clients. There is clearly a serious criminal element operating in the suburb.

No arrests have been made.

PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR – ROB BYGRAVE
Bygrave was employed by one of the other cases – not linked to ADT that occurred earlier in September – he has since been investigating the string of hits – connecting the dots and piecing the modus operandi together.

FINAL SCRIPT

VO: The affluent Johannesburg suburb of Bryanston is being hit hard by a gang of gunwielding criminals - targeting homes, making off with high value movable items.

ROB: they're becoming brazen, they're becoming arrogant and they're getting away with it.

VO: On Tuesday, 84 year-old Peter Hinton-Green’s home was broken into in broad daylight. He was physically assaulted by the robbers who ransacked his home.

His tenant, Cheryl Ducray was out and arrived home shortly after the robbery.

DEREK: Seem fairly calm maybe the shock hasn't really set in.
CHERYL: // we've had too many break ins in Bryanston area that I kept thinking you know it's bound to happen you know one day.

VO: Andre Snyman runs eBlockWatch, an online crime fighting community – he was at the scene when we arrived.

ANDRE: // You can see there's no forced entry. It hasn't been lifted. Every place if we go to know they say they don't know how they got in. It's the first thing they say. How did they get in?

VO: There have been Seven break-ins in 5 weeks . All in Bryanston. All with no signs of forced entry. All Fidelity-ADT Security clients. All had false alarms recently.

ROB: Without a shadow of a doubt this is organized. It's strategic it's direct.

VO: Private Investigator Rob Bygrave has been working cases in Bryanston – while there have been some other incidents, not related to Fidelity-ADT Security. In these cases a trend appears to be emerging.

ROB: // access has been gained via the codes and we have video proof. The guys are coming in knowing what they want and they go into specific residences and passing other residences which means they've got inside information

VO: This is a clip from an incident in October – a man is standing at the access keypad, he punches in a code and just seconds later the gate opens up – letting his accomplices in.

Security companies usually have these codes for the external perimeter, in order to respond when an alarm is activated. These codes are unique to each property.

LINK: Your security is only as good as your weakest link and when that link in the chain is your security company – what chance to you stand against armed criminals?

KAREN: It was a horrific. It was absolutely horrific. I don't ever want us to go through that again.

VO: As far as we know, The Bouic’s were the first to be hit by this gang. On the evening of the 16th of September, Karen, her husband Patrice and their two teenaged children were at held up in their home.

KAREN: Derek. It was surreal. In that moment when this when it happened and I our dog started barking frantically and I saw motion at our front door. And before we know it there was five people in our home

VO: From their neighbour’s CCTV cameras , it appears that the men came in using the access code on the keypad.

Watch carefully as a man stands at the wall where the keypad is fitted, the gate only opens pedestrian width and the men dressed in black enter the property.

LINK: Cameras, high walls, electric fencing re-enforced gates – not gonna help if the criminals have this code on your keypad.

VO: Amy van Heerden’s property is in a complex of four units, just minutes from the Bouic’s home.

This footage is from a break-in two weeks. Watch as a man walks up to the keypad, and types in the access code from a note. The gate also opened pedestrian width, allowing the robbers to enter on foot.

AMY: // We've even asked the suppliers, you know, if it's possible to override that that some way to over ride according to them it's not. You've got to have the code.
DEREK: Who do you think would have known those codes?
AMY: Only the security company because Only three of us has got domestic workers. They do not have this code.

VO: Once through the gate, the robbers moved through the complex quickly.

AMY: I think it was targeted. I think they had the code absolutely for the main gate and house number one. So they walked past my gate very fast. That also passed the next house. They went right to the top gate

VO: But as the armed men got in, the alarm went off and they retreated. Watch how brazen they are – when the owner deactivates the alarm, the robbers come back in – triggering the alarm a second time.

Fidelity-ADT is contracted to around 3300 homes in Bryanston. We spoke the group CEO, Wahl Bartmann this week from Japan.

DEREK: The gates only open pedestrian width no forced entry - can you explain that ?
WAHL: Well to enter, Somebody must have the codes. The million dollar question is who gave them those codes. I don't know if it's been given to anybody but do domestics or gardeners or anybody else. We are investigating it. If it's a leak on our side we need to find out exactly where it is.

VO: While the Bouic’s staff did have the code, they have been polygraphed and cleared . The family has cancelled their contract with Fidelity-ADT.

KAREN: we believed that we were safe in our own home.

VO: But that was not the case, they were threatened, tied up and forced to lie on the ground while the robbers worked through their belongings – taking electronics, jewellery, clothes, shoes, the CCTV recorder and even Karen’s c ar.

KAREN: They systematically went through our home room for room and took what they needed and what they wanted - very professional
DEREK: How did they handle your family.
KAREN: They were very aggressive towards Patrice. They demanded access to the safes.

VO: Even though Patrice didn’t resist or try to fight them, he was physically assaulted.

PATRICE: He started off by saying – “I don’t like you” and he smashed me in the forehead, he smashed me on the ear and the back of my head – quite a few times and then he jumped on my hand.

VO: Battered and bruised, Patrice’s had to undergo surgery on his hand.

KAREN: I'm angry because if something had been done after our incident, if they had just gone out to their clients and said please change the codes on your gate we suspect that there could be a problem, They didn't do it.

VO: Six break-ins targeting Fidelity-ADT clients followed the Bouic robbery. In three separate incidents - one homeowner was severely beaten , another was shot in the shoulder and another’s skull was cracked .

WAHL: I think that the trauma that people go through with the robbery is really we need to apologize and we have to do everything to make sure that we keep you safe and secure your assets.

VO: The notifications warning clients of this particular modus operandi only went out this week – some received emails or text messages, while some were also called directly by Fidelity-ADT.

DEREK: But a number of your clients are saying it's too little too late
WAHL: Looking back. Yes. Can we do things better. Yes. Well we do better. Yes. And I think we have learned from this and the way that we do this and how we can be proactive.

VO: But this is not the first time security access of Fidelity-ADT clients’ homes has been compromised. In July 2018, Kegan Murphy’s 5 year-old daughter, domestic helper and gardener were held up in his home on the outskirts of Bryanston .

KEGAN: Look I don't think security was ever a jeopardy. You know we got electric fencing going all the way around. We were trailing doors burglar bars all the way around beams . But we had someone just with a key walk straight in.

VO: The robbers gained access with a masterkey for a special lock fitted by the security company. The investigation revealed one of the robbers was an ex-ADT employee – he was arrested and is currently on trial.

DEREK: Absolve ex-employee
KEGAN: Absolutely not. // whether it's a current employee or an ex employee who has had access to My personal house’s key.// somebody must be accountable for this key being out of circulation.

DEREK: If you've known of security breaches seemingly involving your employees since 2018. Why haven't you done more about it?
WAHL: Well we've been investigating and then it was a quiet period. Nothing happened. There's been arrests of people. We believe that we've dealt with that matter and the basis that we implemented that that was sufficient.

LINK: But when it comes to putting criminals behind bars, it’s actually the job of the police to investigate cases, collect evidence and identify the suspects.

VO: Currently the Bryanston Break-ins are still only being investigated at police station level according to Brigadier Mathapelo Peters.

BRIG PETERS: Given the increase in these robberies it is a bit concerning for the police so we may even have to escalate it to our organized crime and provincial office.
DEREK: Because surely with the spate of violent attacks you need to escalate it.
BRIG PETERS: Yeah definitely if we do find that it has to be it will be.

VO: In the meantime, Bartmann has appointed a specialised internal team to investigate these cases and possible internal breaches.

The group is also in the final development stages of one-time-pin system that will generate a new pin every time access is required, but as it stands Fidelity -ADT has increased its presence in the area.

WAHL: we've deployed additional resources as well as air support to that area to make sure that we can add more value and make sure that we prevent these incidents

VO: But clients like Amy van Heerden are taking extra measures, chaining her gates.

AMY: We are so vigilant. But it's a false sense of security if you can’t trust your security company.





PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: A series of house break-ins in five weeks in one wealthy Johannesburg suburb. No forced entry, and all clients of the same security company. Could this be a serious secuirty breach?

PROMO 2
VO: Robbers target specific homes all contracted to one security company in a wealthy Johannesburg suburb – Is this a simple security breach or criminals acting on insider information?

PROMO 3
VO: We investigate how a series of break-ins in a wealthy Johannesburg suburb may be the result of a breach in security at the very security company hired to protect residents.

Details Back references from Insert in Show: Title Author Last Updated 03 November 2019 - Carte Blanche HD mihle@combinedartists.co.za 02 December 2019 Script: FINAL SCRIPT VO: The affluent Johannesburg suburb of Bryanston is being hit hard by a gang of gunwielding criminals - targeting homes, making off with high value movable items. ROB: they're becoming brazen, they're becoming arrogant and they're getting away with it. VO: On Tuesday, 84 year-old Peter Hinton-Green’s home was broken into in broad daylight. He was physically assaulted by the robbers who ransacked his home. His tenant, Cheryl Ducray was out and arrived home shortly after the robbery. DEREK: Seem fairly calm maybe the shock hasn't really set in. CHERYL: // we've had too many break ins in Bryanston area that I kept thinking you know it's bound to happen you know one day. VO: Andre Snyman runs eBlockWatch, an online crime fighting community – he was at the scene when we arrived. ANDRE: // You can see there's no forced entry. It hasn't been lifted. Every place if we go to know they say they don't know how they got in. It's the first thing they say. How did they get in? VO: There have been Seven break-ins in 5 weeks . All in Bryanston. All with no signs of forced entry. All Fidelity-ADT Security clients. All had false alarms recently. ROB: Without a shadow of a doubt this is organized. It's strategic it's direct. VO: Private Investigator Rob Bygrave has been working cases in Bryanston – while there have been some other incidents, not related to Fidelity-ADT Security. In these cases a trend appears to be emerging. ROB: // access has been gained via the codes and we have video proof. The guys are coming in knowing what they want and they go into specific residences and passing other residences which means they've got inside information VO: This is a clip from an incident in October – a man is standing at the access keypad, he punches in a code and just seconds later the gate opens up – letting his accomplices in. Security companies usually have these codes for the external perimeter, in order to respond when an alarm is activated. These codes are unique to each property. LINK: Your security is only as good as your weakest link and when that link in the chain is your security company – what chance to you stand against armed criminals? KAREN: It was a horrific. It was absolutely horrific. I don't ever want us to go through that again. VO: As far as we know, The Bouic’s were the first to be hit by this gang. On the evening of the 16th of September, Karen, her husband Patrice and their two teenaged children were at held up in their home. KAREN: Derek. It was surreal. In that moment when this when it happened and I our dog started barking frantically and I saw motion at our front door. And before we know it there was five people in our home VO: From their neighbour’s CCTV cameras , it appears that the men came in using the access code on the keypad. Watch carefully as a man stands at the wall where the keypad is fitted, the gate only opens pedestrian width and the men dressed in black enter the property. LINK: Cameras, high walls, electric fencing re-enforced gates – not gonna help if the criminals have this code on your keypad. VO: Amy van Heerden’s property is in a complex of four units, just minutes from the Bouic’s home. This footage is from a break-in two weeks. Watch as a man walks up to the keypad, and types in the access code from a note. The gate also opened pedestrian width, allowing the robbers to enter on foot. AMY: // We've even asked the suppliers, you know, if it's possible to override that that some way to over ride according to them it's not. You've got to have the code. DEREK: Who do you think would have known those codes? AMY: Only the security company because Only three of us has got domestic workers. They do not have this code. VO: Once through the gate, the robbers moved through the complex quickly. AMY: I think it was targeted. I think they had the code absolutely for the main gate and house number one. So they walked past my gate very fast. That also passed the next house. They went right to the top gate VO: But as the armed men got in, the alarm went off and they retreated. Watch how brazen they are – when the owner deactivates the alarm, the robbers come back in – triggering the alarm a second time. Fidelity-ADT is contracted to around 3300 homes in Bryanston. We spoke the group CEO, Wahl Bartmann this week from Japan. DEREK: The gates only open pedestrian width no forced entry - can you explain that ? WAHL: Well to enter, Somebody must have the codes. The million dollar question is who gave them those codes. I don't know if it's been given to anybody but do domestics or gardeners or anybody else. We are investigating it. If it's a leak on our side we need to find out exactly where it is. VO: While the Bouic’s staff did have the code, they have been polygraphed and cleared . The family has cancelled their contract with Fidelity-ADT. KAREN: we believed that we were safe in our own home. VO: But that was not the case, they were threatened, tied up and forced to lie on the ground while the robbers worked through their belongings – taking electronics, jewellery, clothes, shoes, the CCTV recorder and even Karen’s c ar. KAREN: They systematically went through our home room for room and took what they needed and what they wanted - very professional DEREK: How did they handle your family. KAREN: They were very aggressive towards Patrice. They demanded access to the safes. VO: Even though Patrice didn’t resist or try to fight them, he was physically assaulted. PATRICE: He started off by saying – “I don’t like you” and he smashed me in the forehead, he smashed me on the ear and the back of my head – quite a few times and then he jumped on my hand. VO: Battered and bruised, Patrice’s had to undergo surgery on his hand. KAREN: I'm angry because if something had been done after our incident, if they had just gone out to their clients and said please change the codes on your gate we suspect that there could be a problem, They didn't do it. VO: Six break-ins targeting Fidelity-ADT clients followed the Bouic robbery. In three separate incidents - one homeowner was severely beaten , another was shot in the shoulder and another’s skull was cracked . WAHL: I think that the trauma that people go through with the robbery is really we need to apologize and we have to do everything to make sure that we keep you safe and secure your assets. VO: The notifications warning clients of this particular modus operandi only went out this week – some received emails or text messages, while some were also called directly by Fidelity-ADT. DEREK: But a number of your clients are saying it's too little too late WAHL: Looking back. Yes. Can we do things better. Yes. Well we do better. Yes. And I think we have learned from this and the way that we do this and how we can be proactive. VO: But this is not the first time security access of Fidelity-ADT clients’ homes has been compromised. In July 2018, Kegan Murphy’s 5 year-old daughter, domestic helper and gardener were held up in his home on the outskirts of Bryanston . KEGAN: Look I don't think security was ever a jeopardy. You know we got electric fencing going all the way around. We were trailing doors burglar bars all the way around beams . But we had someone just with a key walk straight in. VO: The robbers gained access with a masterkey for a special lock fitted by the security company. The investigation revealed one of the robbers was an ex-ADT employee – he was arrested and is currently on trial. DEREK: Absolve ex-employee KEGAN: Absolutely not. // whether it's a current employee or an ex employee who has had access to My personal house’s key.// somebody must be accountable for this key being out of circulation. DEREK: If you've known of security breaches seemingly involving your employees since 2018. Why haven't you done more about it? WAHL: Well we've been investigating and then it was a quiet period. Nothing happened. There's been arrests of people. We believe that we've dealt with that matter and the basis that we implemented that that was sufficient. LINK: But when it comes to putting criminals behind bars, it’s actually the job of the police to investigate cases, collect evidence and identify the suspects. VO: Currently the Bryanston Break-ins are still only being investigated at police station level according to Brigadier Mathapelo Peters. BRIG PETERS: Given the increase in these robberies it is a bit concerning for the police so we may even have to escalate it to our organized crime and provincial office. DEREK: Because surely with the spate of violent attacks you need to escalate it. BRIG PETERS: Yeah definitely if we do find that it has to be it will be. VO: In the meantime, Bartmann has appointed a specialised internal team to investigate these cases and possible internal breaches. The group is also in the final development stages of one-time-pin system that will generate a new pin every time access is required, but as it stands Fidelity -ADT has increased its presence in the area. WAHL: we've deployed additional resources as well as air support to that area to make sure that we can add more value and make sure that we prevent these incidents VO: But clients like Amy van Heerden are taking extra measures, chaining her gates. AMY: We are so vigilant. But it's a false sense of security if you can’t trust your security company. PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: A series of house break-ins in five weeks in one wealthy Johannesburg suburb. No forced entry, and all clients of the same security company. Could this be a serious secuirty breach? PROMO 2 VO: Robbers target specific homes all contracted to one security company in a wealthy Johannesburg suburb – Is this a simple security breach or criminals acting on insider information? PROMO 3 VO: We investigate how a series of break-ins in a wealthy Johannesburg suburb may be the result of a breach in security at the very security company hired to protect residents. metadata.Summary: Seven Robberies in 5 weeks. All in Bryanston. All between 19.00 & 20.00 at night. All no forced entry. All access gained via keypad or locking mechanism at the remote gate. All ADT Security clients. It appears that there is a leak within the security company. We investigate, connect the dots and put ADT and the cops in the hotseat.
metadata.Further information: Out of 10 robberies since the middle of September in Bryanston – 7 of the incidents were clients of ADT Security – there was no forced entry and the criminals enter the properties using codes on the keypad at the remote gates of the properties. The conclusion is that information is being leaked from ADT. All these incidents happen between 19.00 & 20.00 – most people have just had dinner and have not armed the security alarm system yet for the night. In some incidents the victims have been injured. A man’s hand was broken, another was shot in the shoulder and a third man had his skull cracked and had to undergo surgery. The criminals usually wear balaclavas, come in with guns, demand electronics, money, jewellery and have made off with two cars from the properties they have robbed. CASE STUDY 1: KAREN BOUIC 16 Sept 2019 – Karen was held up with her family – the gang came in around 19.30, they gained access using the keypad on the gate. They spent 45 minutes in the house and got away with electronics, jewelry, clothes and took Karen’s Hyundai i20. They suspect it was inside job. FROM HER HUSBAND: I had the traumatic event of having five armed men wearing balaclavas enter our house and hold us hostage for 45 minutes. I was beaten when I went to show them where the safe was and the one violent individual jumped on my hand and broke a metacarpal. I had to have four pins put in to hold it together. I cannot begin to tell you how this affected everyone and what thoughts went through my family’s minds during the 45 minutes where these robbers ransacked the house. The point of this story is that these guys entered our property by using our keypad at the gate. We were guarded by Fidelty-ADT and, two events took place in the previous weeks of the armed robbery. Our alarm went off two weeks prior and an ADT security guard came onto our premises whilst we were not at home. Four days before the incident, we called ADT in to do some additional work on the alarm system and the salesperson (Mark Schoeman) wrote up a contract where he transcribed our Digipad code onto the sales document. We never gave him that code, so the implication is that this information is freely available within their organization. We have met with ADT over 3 weeks ago and they agreed to do polygraph tests on their staff which has now come back negative. There have now been five armed and violent incidents in the Bryanston area in the last four weeks where the mode of operation has been to access the property using the keypad. We know with certainty that three of the properties were guarded by ADT who ad access to the gate codes, and we are still to confirm the other two. CASE STUDY 2: AMY VAN HEERDEN This happened in Bryanston, 51 Saint James Crescent on Monday 14 Oct 20:05. The perps went through the main complex gate by using the ADT digipad (Video 1). They then went to the top house (house number 1 is at the top) and entered another gate also using the digipad. In Video 2 you can see the 4 perps passing Amy’s gate and digipad (2nd house in the complex) with no interest. The criminals went straight for Unit 1 – it is clear it was a targeted incident. The alarm at unit 1 was already armed when the criminals tried to gain access. They eventually retreated - they left after the alarm was triggered, opening the main gate again with the digipad. There are 4 houses in the complex, with 3 of them using ADT. THIS IS AN EXAMPLE OF A TARGETED ROBBERY ATTEMPT – THE ROBBERS CAME IN AND HEADED STRAIGHT FOR THE HOUSE THAT THEY HAD THE KEYPAD FOR. THIS INFO HAS BEEN SHARED WITH ADT BY THE CLIENTS, TO DATE NO RESPONSE. ADT KNOW ABOUT THE ISSUE ADT are aware of the possible breach – but it appears nothing is being done. No notifications have been sent out to clients informing them of the possible breach or advising them to change their access codes. The robberies continue – just last week there were two. ADT admitted to one victim that they were aware of the issue and advised him not the give his new access codes to the ADT control centre. ADT’s RESPONSE TO KAREN BOUIC: “All employees interviewed and polygraphed, at this stage, denied any involvement in the incident whatsoever and were found to be truthful when answering the relevant questions and advised by the investigator that they be excluded as suspects during any further investigation into the matter. Regarding the process pertaining to digipad code access during activations, upon receipt of an activation the customer’s digipad access code can only be accessed after entering the customer’s password into the system. The Control Room Operator has to obtain the password from the customers. Once a Reaction Officer is dispatched to the premises the digipad access code is displayed on the vehicle unit (Tom-Tom) in order for the officer to gain access. Once the activation is cancelled or completed the access code is no longer visible to the officer. This process ensures that codes are kept secure.” BUT it is possible that the code can be written down, a picture can be taken or someone in the control room could have given out the info as they have access to the codes. The majorit of the 7 ADT cases had a false alarm of sorts in the weeks leading up to the robberies. CASE STUDY 3: KEGAN MURPHY In 2018 Kegan Murphy was robbed, also Bryanston. The criminals gained access during the day using a master key for the remote gate that was in the possession of ADT Security. His helper, gardener and 5 year old daughter were held up in the home. Arrests were made, after ADT Security ID-ed one of the men as an ex-ADT employee. He is currently on trial. Kegan is furious – ADT management admitted responsibility and offered to pay for the replacement lock. His daughter has had to go to play therapy following the traumatic incident. SINCE 2018 ADT HAVE BEEN AWARE OF SECURITY BREACHES. THE COPS There at least two other gangs at work in the area at the moment as well. The other gangs access by breaking the gates or jumping walls, they crawl across the gardens under the security beams and then usually remove windows to get into the house. There have also been other robberies not linked to ADT clients. There is clearly a serious criminal element operating in the suburb. No arrests have been made. PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR – ROB BYGRAVE Bygrave was employed by one of the other cases – not linked to ADT that occurred earlier in September – he has since been investigating the string of hits – connecting the dots and piecing the modus operandi together.
